state.name: New York
state.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
state.peak_intrusion_season: Late September through November as raccoons, squirrels, and bats seek winter shelter, February through April for raccoon and squirrel denning, and spring through summer for bat maternity colonies, groundhog and skunk emergence, and mole lawn damage
state.climate_factor: New York's hard continental winters push rodents, squirrels, and bats into heated attics, lake-effect snow belts off Lakes Erie and Ontario bury the Buffalo, Rochester, and Syracuse corridors, and milder coastal-moderated winters on Long Island and in New York City keep rats, raccoons, and pigeons active year-round downstate
state.permit_note: New York requires anyone charging a fee for nuisance wildlife work to hold a nuisance wildlife control operator (NWCO) license issued by DEC under Environmental Conservation Law section 11-0524; that license does not cover deer, bear, beaver, otter, mink, muskrat, fisher, bobcat, wild turkey, native snakes or turtles, endangered or threatened species, or migratory birds, which need special DEC or federal permits, and homeowners may not relocate wildlife off their own property

Albany County.region: the Capital District on the upper Hudson River
Albany County.nearest_metro: Albany is itself the regional metro center
Albany County.habitat_type: state-capital neighborhoods, older river cities, and dense suburbs under mature canopy
Albany County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold the older blocks of Albany, Cohoes, and Watervliet, raccoons and squirrels work the Pine Bush-edge suburbs of Colonie and Guilderland, and bats return to big older homes in Bethlehem each summer
Albany County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, and fishers live in the Helderberg and river-edge woods around the county but need special DEC permits and are handled through the regional DEC wildlife office, not as a routine booking

Allegany County.region: the Southern Tier along the Pennsylvania line
Allegany County.nearest_metro: Jamestown and Olean to the west, Rochester to the north
Allegany County.habitat_type: rural farm and forest country with small villages and seasonal camps
Allegany County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the farm fields and garden edges around Wellsville and Cuba, raccoons and bats settle older farmhouses and camps, and skunks work under porches across the small villages
Allegany County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, bobcats, and fishers are present in the county's deep woods but are permit-gated species referred to DEC, never a private removal service

Bronx County.region: the northernmost New York City borough, on the mainland north of Manhattan
Bronx County.habitat_type: dense mainland borough of pre-war apartment buildings, rowhouses, and parkland
Bronx County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats run the older apartment blocks and commercial corridors, raccoons work Pelham Bay and Van Cortlandt park edges into Riverdale yards, and pigeons and starlings nest in signs, bridges, and roof structures borough-wide
Bronx County.absent_or_rare: coyotes are seen in the borough's big parks and deer appear at the northern edge, but neither is a private removal job in New York City — sightings go to the city and DEC

Broome County.region: the eastern Southern Tier at the Susquehanna and Chenango river confluence
Broome County.nearest_metro: Binghamton is itself the regional metro center
Broome County.habitat_type: a river-valley metro of older mill and shoe-factory housing ringed by wooded hills
Broome County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Binghamton, Johnson City, and Endicott's older blocks, raccoons and squirrels fill Triple Cities attics each fall, and groundhogs burrow the hillside yards above the river valley
Broome County.absent_or_rare: black bears come down from the surrounding hills into bird feeders and trash in spring, but bears are a DEC matter requiring a special permit, not a booking

Cattaraugus County.region: the western Southern Tier, home to Allegany State Park
Cattaraugus County.habitat_type: forested hills, ski country, and small river towns
Cattaraugus County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm and village edges around Olean and Randolph, raccoons and bats settle seasonal homes near Ellicottville and Allegany State Park, and squirrels fill camp attics left empty all winter
Cattaraugus County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, bobcats, and fishers are common in Allegany State Park country but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Cayuga County.region: the northern Finger Lakes on Owasco and Cayuga lakes
Cayuga County.habitat_type: lake towns, farmland, and marsh country between two Finger Lakes
Cayuga County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are steady in Auburn's older housing, groundhogs burrow farm edges from Moravia to Weedsport, and skunks den under lake cottages around Owasco and Cayuga lakes
Cayuga County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the Montezuma marsh edges and lake outlets, but both need special DEC permits and are referred to the regional DEC office

Chautauqua County.region: the far western corner of the state on Lake Erie
Chautauqua County.nearest_metro: Buffalo (about 70 miles northeast) and Erie, Pennsylvania
Chautauqua County.habitat_type: grape-belt lake towns, a small manufacturing city, and farm and forest interior
Chautauqua County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and pigeons hold older Jamestown and Dunkirk blocks, raccoons and squirrels work the Chautauqua Lake cottage belt, and groundhogs burrow the grape-farm edges from Fredonia to Westfield
Chautauqua County.absent_or_rare: beavers flood interior creek bottoms and black bears wander the southern hills, but both are permit-gated species handled through DEC

Chemung County.region: the central Southern Tier on the Chemung River
Chemung County.nearest_metro: Elmira is itself the regional metro center
Chemung County.habitat_type: a river-valley city of older industrial housing with wooded hillsides
Chemung County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Elmira's older neighborhoods, raccoons and squirrels take hillside attics in Elmira Heights and Horseheads, and groundhogs and skunks work the garden suburbs of Big Flats and Southport
Chemung County.absent_or_rare: black bears descend from the southern hills in spring and beavers work the Chemung River backwaters, but both need special DEC permits

Chenango County.region: the central Southern Tier river valleys
Chenango County.habitat_type: rolling dairy-farm valleys and small river towns
Chenango County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs are a constant on dairy-farm edges and garden plots from Norwich to Oxford, raccoons and bats settle older farmhouses, and skunks den under village porches each spring
Chenango County.absent_or_rare: beavers, fishers, and black bears are established in the county's forests but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Clinton County.region: the northeastern corner on Lake Champlain and the Canadian border
Clinton County.nearest_metro: Plattsburgh is the regional center; Montreal is about 60 miles north
Clinton County.habitat_type: a lake port city, farmland, and the Adirondack foothills
Clinton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels work Plattsburgh's older neighborhoods and lake camps, groundhogs burrow Champlain-valley farm edges, and bats colonize older homes in Peru and Dannemora each summer
Clinton County.absent_or_rare: moose wander the western towns and beavers and fishers work the interior woods, but all are DEC-managed species, not private removal work

Columbia County.region: the east bank of the mid-Hudson Valley
Columbia County.habitat_type: river city, farm valleys, and second-home country under the Taconics
Columbia County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats fill the older homes and weekend houses of Hudson, Kinderhook, and Chatham, groundhogs burrow farm and garden edges county-wide, and skunks den under barns and porches
Columbia County.absent_or_rare: black bears and bobcats move through the Taconic foothills and beavers work the Kinderhook Creek bottoms, but all are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Cortland County.region: the gateway between the Finger Lakes and the Southern Tier
Cortland County.nearest_metro: Syracuse (about 35 miles north) and Binghamton (about 40 miles south)
Cortland County.habitat_type: a small college and manufacturing city in a farm valley
Cortland County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the valley farm edges, raccoons and squirrels take Cortland and Homer attics, and bats return to older village homes each summer
Cortland County.absent_or_rare: beavers and fishers work the Tioughnioga corridor and upland forests but need special DEC permits

Delaware County.region: the western Catskills and the Delaware River headwaters
natural_features: East and West Branches of the Delaware River
Delaware County.habitat_type: mountain farm valleys, reservoir country, and seasonal homes
Delaware County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats settle seasonal Catskill homes left empty for weeks, groundhogs burrow the farm valleys around Delhi and Walton, and skunks work under porches in the river villages
Delaware County.absent_or_rare: black bears are a fixture of the western Catskills and beavers and bobcats work the reservoir feeder streams, but all are permit-gated DEC species

Dutchess County.region: the east bank of the mid-Hudson Valley, a New York City commuter county
Dutchess County.nearest_metro: Poughkeepsie and Beacon anchor the county; New York City is about 75 miles south
Dutchess County.habitat_type: a river city, commuter suburbs, and horse-farm and estate country
Dutchess County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and pigeons hold older Poughkeepsie blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the commuter suburbs of Fishkill, Wappinger, and Hyde Park, and bats and groundhogs are steady on the farm and estate properties around Rhinebeck
Dutchess County.absent_or_rare: black bears cross the eastern hills and beavers work the Wappinger and Ten Mile creek bottoms, but both need special DEC permits; copperheads occur in the rocky Hudson Highlands at the county's southern edge — identification and safety only

Erie County.region: the Lake Erie and Niagara River shore of western New York
Erie County.nearest_metro: Buffalo is itself the regional metro center
Erie County.habitat_type: a Great Lakes port metro of older industrial neighborhoods and dense suburbs - lake-effect snow belts, older housing, and heavy suburban canopy
Erie County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold Buffalo and Lackawanna's older industrial blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the Amherst, Tonawanda, and Cheektowaga suburbs, groundhogs and skunks work the Hamburg and West Seneca yard edges, and bats colonize older homes across the metro each summer
Erie County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the Buffalo Creek and Tonawanda Creek bottoms but need special DEC permits, and deer in the metro parks are a DEC matter, not a booking

Essex County.region: the Adirondack High Peaks and Lake Champlain
Essex County.habitat_type: mountain and lake country of camps, second homes, and small towns
Essex County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats settle Adirondack camps and second homes around Lake Placid and Keene that sit empty for weeks, squirrels fill camp attics each fall, and groundhogs work the Champlain-valley farms
Essex County.absent_or_rare: moose, black bears, beavers, fishers, and bobcats are Adirondack fixtures but are DEC-managed, permit-gated species; Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in the county, so bat work is identification and exclusion only

Franklin County.region: the northern Adirondacks and the St. Lawrence valley edge
Franklin County.habitat_type: northern forest, lake camps, and farm towns
Franklin County.regional_wildlife: bats and squirrels overwinter in Saranac Lake and Tupper Lake camps, raccoons work Malone's older housing, and skunks and groundhogs are steady on the farm edges
Franklin County.absent_or_rare: moose, black bears, beavers, and fishers are common in the northern woods but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Fulton County.region: the southern Adirondack foothills and Mohawk valley edge
Fulton County.nearest_metro: Albany (about 45 miles southeast) via the Mohawk valley
Fulton County.habitat_type: glove-city housing, foothill towns, and a large reservoir lake belt
Fulton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats settle Great Sacandaga Lake camps and older Johnstown and Gloversville homes, and groundhogs burrow the foothill farm edges
Fulton County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, and fishers work the foothill forests but need special DEC permits

Genesee County.region: the flat farm plain between Buffalo and Rochester
Genesee County.nearest_metro: Buffalo (about 35 miles west) and Rochester (about 35 miles east)
Genesee County.habitat_type: a small manufacturing city surrounded by rich muck and dairy farmland
Genesee County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the farm and ditch-bank edges from Le Roy to Pavilion, raccoons and squirrels take Batavia attics, and Norway rats persist in Batavia's older commercial blocks
Genesee County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats work the Tonawanda and Oak Orchard creek bottoms and the refuge marshes, but both are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Greene County.region: the northern Catskills and the west bank of the Hudson
Greene County.habitat_type: river towns, ski-mountain villages, and seasonal Catskill homes
Greene County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats settle seasonal homes around Windham and Hunter, squirrels fill Catskill and Coxsackie attics, and groundhogs burrow the valley farms
Greene County.absent_or_rare: black bears are routine in the northern Catskills and beavers work the creek bottoms, but both are permit-gated DEC species; timber rattlesnakes occur at the edges of the eastern Catskills — safety and identification only

Hamilton County.region: the heart of the Adirondack Park, the state's least populous county
Hamilton County.nearest_metro: Utica and Glens Falls are the nearest small metros, each over an hour away
Hamilton County.habitat_type: deep-forest lake camps and hamlets inside the Adirondack Park
Hamilton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the main camp problem, settling roofs and chimneys of seasonal homes around Speculator, Indian Lake, and Long Lake that sit empty most of the year
Hamilton County.absent_or_rare: moose, black bears, beavers, fishers, and bobcats define this county's wildlife but are all DEC-managed and permit-gated

Herkimer County.region: the Mohawk valley and southern Adirondacks
Herkimer County.habitat_type: mill villages along the Mohawk with Adirondack foothill towns north
Herkimer County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and raccoons work the older mill housing of Ilion, Herkimer, and Little Falls, groundhogs burrow valley farm edges, and bats settle foothill camps to the north
Herkimer County.absent_or_rare: beavers, fishers, and black bears work the West Canada Creek corridor and northern woods but need special DEC permits

Jefferson County.region: the Lake Ontario and St. Lawrence River shore, including the Thousand Islands
Jefferson County.nearest_metro: Watertown is itself the regional center; Syracuse is about 70 miles south
natural_features: St. Lawrence River and Thousand Islands
Jefferson County.habitat_type: a river-and-lake city, military-adjacent suburbs near Fort Drum, and island and farm country
Jefferson County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats settle Watertown homes and Thousand Islands cottages around Clayton and Alexandria Bay, Norway rats hold Watertown's older blocks, and groundhogs burrow the farm interior
Jefferson County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the Black River and lakeshore marshes and Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in the county, so those cases are permit and DEC matters, not routine bookings

Kings County.region: the western end of Long Island, New York City's most populous borough
Kings County.habitat_type: a dense borough of brownstones, rowhouses, pre-war apartments, and warehouses
Kings County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are the borough's number-one call, running brownstone basements, restaurant rows, and older apartment blocks, pigeons and house sparrows nest in signs, cornices, and roof structures, and raccoons and squirrels work the Prospect Park and Green-Wood edges into Park Slope and Bay Ridge yards
Kings County.absent_or_rare: Canada geese gather on Jamaica Bay and park lawns but need federal authorization for any control work, so goose problems are deterrence and habitat work only

Lewis County.region: the Tug Hill plateau and Black River valley
Lewis County.habitat_type: deep-snow farm and forest country of small villages
Lewis County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the dairy-farm edges around Lowville and Croghan, and raccoons and bats settle older farmhouses and Tug Hill camps
Lewis County.absent_or_rare: beavers, fishers, bobcats, and black bears are established on the Tug Hill but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Livingston County.region: the Genesee River valley and western Finger Lakes edge
Livingston County.habitat_type: college and farm towns around a finger lake
Livingston County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the rich valley farmland, raccoons and bats settle Geneseo and Dansville homes, and skunks den under porches in the lake towns around Conesus
Livingston County.absent_or_rare: beavers work the Genesee River bottoms and black bears pass through the southern hills, but both need special DEC permits

Madison County.region: the geographic center of the state, between Syracuse and Utica
Madison County.nearest_metro: Syracuse (about 25 miles west) and Utica (about 25 miles east)
Madison County.habitat_type: farm towns, a small city, and lake communities
Madison County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm and garden edges from Canastota to Hamilton, raccoons and bats take older homes in Oneida and Cazenovia, and squirrels fill attics each fall
Madison County.absent_or_rare: the eastern massasauga's central New York bog country lies just west of the county and beavers work the Oneida Creek bottoms — the snake is state-Endangered and safety-only, and beaver work is permit-gated

Monroe County.region: the Lake Ontario shore of the Genesee River
Monroe County.nearest_metro: Rochester is itself the regional metro center
Monroe County.habitat_type: a Great Lakes industrial metro of older city housing and leafy suburbs - lake-effect snow, canal corridors, and dense older housing stock
Monroe County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Rochester's older neighborhoods, raccoons and squirrels fill attics from Greece and Irondequoit to Pittsford and Henrietta, groundhogs burrow the canal-side and farm edges, and bats return to big older homes each summer under heavy lake-effect snow
Monroe County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats work the Braddock Bay marshes and canal bottoms but are permit-gated and referred to DEC; deer are abundant in the metro parks but are a DEC matter

Montgomery County.region: the Mohawk valley west of Albany
Montgomery County.nearest_metro: Albany (about 40 miles east) and Utica (about 45 miles west)
Montgomery County.habitat_type: canal and mill towns in a farm valley
Montgomery County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and raccoons hold Amsterdam's older mill blocks, groundhogs burrow the valley farms, and bats and squirrels settle homes from Canajoharie to St. Johnsville
Montgomery County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats work the Mohawk River backwaters and creek bottoms but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Nassau County.region: the western half of Long Island, directly east of New York City
Nassau County.habitat_type: dense post-war suburbs, Gold Coast estates, and older downtown villages
Nassau County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels are the dominant attic calls from Great Neck to Garden City, Norway rats hold the older downtowns of Hempstead, Freeport, and Glen Cove, and opossums and bats are steady across the post-war subdivisions
Nassau County.absent_or_rare: Canada geese crowd the county's ponds and golf courses but need federal authorization for control, so goose work is deterrence only; there are no groundhog-heavy farm edges left in most of this built-out county

New York County.region: Manhattan, the island borough between the Hudson and East rivers
New York County.habitat_type: the densest county in America — pre-war high-rises, brownstones, and commercial towers
New York County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats define Manhattan wildlife work, running basements, trash rooms, and restaurant blocks in every neighborhood, pigeons and house sparrows nest on ledges, signs, and AC units, and raccoons and squirrels work Central Park's edges into Upper West and Upper East Side rooflines
New York County.absent_or_rare: peregrine falcons nest on Manhattan bridges and towers and Canada geese use its parks, but protected birds are observation and deterrence matters only, never removal

Niagara County.region: the Niagara River and Lake Ontario shore
Niagara County.habitat_type: a falls city, canal towns, and fruit-belt farmland
Niagara County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and pigeons hold older Niagara Falls and Lockport blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the canal-town suburbs, and groundhogs and skunks work the fruit-belt farm edges from Lewiston to Newfane
Niagara County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the Tonawanda Creek and lakeshore marsh bottoms but need special DEC permits

Oneida County.region: the Mohawk valley and Tug Hill and Adirondack foothills
Oneida County.nearest_metro: Utica and Rome anchor the county; Syracuse is about 55 miles west
Oneida County.habitat_type: an older industrial metro in a river valley with farm and foothill towns
Oneida County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Utica and Rome's older neighborhoods, raccoons and squirrels fill attics in New Hartford, Whitesboro, and Clinton, and groundhogs and skunks work the farm edges county-wide
Oneida County.absent_or_rare: black bears come off the Tug Hill and Adirondack foothills, and beavers work the creek bottoms — both are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Onondaga County.region: the geographic center of the state on Onondaga Lake
Onondaga County.nearest_metro: Syracuse is itself the regional metro center
Onondaga County.habitat_type: a lake-and-canal metro of older city blocks and sprawling northern suburbs - lake-effect snow off Lake Ontario, older salt-city housing, and wooded eastern hills
Onondaga County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold Syracuse's older salt-city blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the Clay, Cicero, and Manlius suburbs, groundhogs and skunks work the yard edges county-wide, and bats settle older homes around Baldwinsville and Liverpool each summer
Onondaga County.absent_or_rare: Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in Onondaga County, so bat colonies are identified before any exclusion is planned; beavers on the Seneca River bottoms are permit-gated, and the eastern massasauga's central New York bog country lies just west - that snake is state-Endangered and safety-only

Ontario County.region: the northern Finger Lakes on Canandaigua and Seneca lakes
Ontario County.habitat_type: growing Rochester exurbs, lake towns, and farm country
Ontario County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the farm and vineyard edges, raccoons and squirrels take the growing Victor and Farmington subdivisions, and bats settle older Canandaigua and Geneva homes
Ontario County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats work the lake outlets and marsh edges but are permit-gated; Geneva sits on the Ontario and Seneca county line, and its Ontario County side is the larger share

Orange County.region: the lower Hudson Valley and the New Jersey and Pennsylvania lines
Orange County.nearest_metro: the New York City metro's outer ring (about 60 miles to Manhattan)
Orange County.habitat_type: a fast-growing commuter county of a small industrial city, suburbs, and farm valleys
Orange County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold older Newburgh and Middletown blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the fast-growing suburbs of Monroe, Warwick, and Goshen, and groundhogs and skunks work the Wallkill valley farm edges
Orange County.absent_or_rare: copperheads and timber rattlesnakes occur in the rocky Highlands and Shawangunk terrain — both are safety and identification matters only, copperheads as a downstate snake and the rattlesnake as a state-Threatened species; black bears are routine here but are a DEC matter

Orleans County.region: the Lake Ontario shore between Buffalo and Rochester
Orleans County.nearest_metro: Buffalo and Rochester are each about 35-40 miles away
Orleans County.habitat_type: canal villages and flat fruit and farm country
Orleans County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm and canal-bank edges, raccoons and bats settle Albion and Medina's older homes, and squirrels fill village attics each fall
Orleans County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the Oak Orchard and marsh bottoms but need special DEC permits

Oswego County.region: the southeastern Lake Ontario shore and Tug Hill edge
Oswego County.habitat_type: a lake port city, river towns, and snowy Tug Hill-edge farm country
Oswego County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold Oswego and Fulton's older river blocks, raccoons and squirrels take homes from Mexico to Phoenix, and groundhogs and skunks work the farm edges under some of the heaviest lake-effect snow in the East
Oswego County.absent_or_rare: Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in the county, so bat colonies are identified before any exclusion is planned; beavers work the Salmon River bottoms but are permit-gated

Otsego County.region: the northern Catskill foothills and Susquehanna headwaters
Otsego County.nearest_metro: Binghamton and Utica are each about 60 miles away
Otsego County.habitat_type: a small college city, a famous lake village, and dairy-farm hills
Otsego County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs are a fixture of the dairy-farm landscape, raccoons and bats settle Oneonta and Cooperstown homes and seasonal lake houses, and skunks den under village porches
Otsego County.absent_or_rare: beavers, fishers, and black bears work the hill forests but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Putnam County.region: the Hudson Highlands east of the river, a New York City commuter county
Putnam County.nearest_metro: the New York City metro (about 60 miles to Manhattan)
Putnam County.habitat_type: wooded commuter towns, reservoir country, and rocky Highlands terrain
Putnam County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels are the steady attic calls in Carmel, Mahopac, and Patterson, bats settle older Cold Spring and Brewster homes, and skunks and groundhogs work the wooded lots county-wide
Putnam County.absent_or_rare: copperheads occur in the rocky Hudson Highlands around Cold Spring — identification and safety only, never a removal promise; black bears and beavers in the watershed woods are DEC matters

Queens County.region: the northwestern Long Island borough of New York City
Queens County.habitat_type: a vast borough of attached rowhouses, garden apartments, and two-family homes
Queens County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats run the older commercial corridors and attached housing from Astoria to Jamaica, raccoons and squirrels work the Forest Park and Flushing Meadows edges into Ridgewood, Glendale, and Forest Hills rooflines, and pigeons nest in elevated-train structures, signs, and roof bulkheads
Queens County.absent_or_rare: Canada geese gather on Jamaica Bay and the park lakes but need federal authorization for any control work, so goose problems are deterrence and habitat work only

Rensselaer County.region: the east bank of the Hudson across from Albany
Rensselaer County.habitat_type: an older mill and college city, commuter suburbs, and rural hill towns east
Rensselaer County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and pigeons hold Troy's older downtown and mill blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the East Greenbush and Brunswick suburbs, and groundhogs and bats are steady in the hill towns toward Grafton
Rensselaer County.absent_or_rare: black bears and beavers work the eastern hills and Hoosic River bottoms but need special DEC permits

Richmond County.region: Staten Island, the southernmost borough, across the harbor from Manhattan
natural_features: Upper and Lower New York Bay
Richmond County.habitat_type: the most suburban borough — single-family homes, townhouses, and the Greenbelt's forest
Richmond County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels are the dominant calls in the island's single-family neighborhoods from St. George to Tottenville, Norway rats hold the older North Shore and Arthur Kill industrial edges, and opossums and bats work the Greenbelt-edge streets
Richmond County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer are a visible presence in the Greenbelt and island parks but deer are a DEC and city matter requiring special permits, never a private removal booking

Rockland County.region: the west bank of the lower Hudson, the smallest county by area in the state outside New York City
Rockland County.nearest_metro: the New York City metro (about 30 miles to Manhattan)
natural_features: Harriman and Bear Mountain State Parks
Rockland County.habitat_type: dense commuter suburbs pressed against state-park forest
Rockland County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels run the dense suburbs of Clarkstown, Spring Valley, and New City where park forest meets rooftops, Norway rats hold older Spring Valley and Haverstraw blocks, and skunks and groundhogs work the yard edges
Rockland County.absent_or_rare: copperheads occur in the rocky Harriman and Bear Mountain terrain — identification and safety only; black bears wander out of the state parks regularly but are a DEC matter, not a booking

Saratoga County.region: the upper Hudson and southern Adirondack foothills north of Albany
Saratoga County.habitat_type: a fast-growing county of a resort city, dense suburbs, and horse country
Saratoga County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels fill attics in fast-growing Clifton Park, Halfmoon, and Malta, Norway rats hold older Mechanicville and Saratoga Springs blocks, and bats and groundhogs are steady around Saratoga Lake and the horse farms
Saratoga County.absent_or_rare: black bears and beavers work the northern foothill towns but need special DEC permits; Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in the wider Capital and cave country, so colonies are identified before exclusion

Schenectady County.region: the Mohawk River in the Capital District
Schenectady County.habitat_type: a compact older industrial city with leafy suburbs and rural edges
Schenectady County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and pigeons hold Schenectady's older downtown and industrial blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the Niskayuna, Rotterdam, and Glenville suburbs, and bats return to big older homes each summer
Schenectady County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats work the Mohawk River and Plotter Kill bottoms but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Schoharie County.region: the Schoharie valley between the Catskills and Capital District
Schoharie County.habitat_type: farm valleys and small villages under Catskill foothills
Schoharie County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the rich valley farmland, raccoons and bats settle Cobleskill and Schoharie village homes, and skunks den under porches and barns
Schoharie County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, and fishers work the foothill forests but are permit-gated DEC species

Schuyler County.region: the southern end of Seneca Lake in the Finger Lakes
Schuyler County.nearest_metro: Elmira (about 20 miles south) and Ithaca (about 20 miles east)
Schuyler County.habitat_type: a gorge and vineyard village, lake cottages, and national-forest farms
Schuyler County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats settle Watkins Glen and Montour Falls homes and lake cottages, and groundhogs and skunks work the farm and vineyard edges
Schuyler County.absent_or_rare: beavers and black bears work the national forest and Hector hills but need special DEC permits

Seneca County.region: between Seneca and Cayuga lakes in the Finger Lakes
Seneca County.nearest_metro: Syracuse, Rochester, and Ithaca are each about 45-55 miles away
Seneca County.habitat_type: two-lake farm country and historic canal towns
Seneca County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm edges between the lakes, raccoons and bats take Seneca Falls and Waterloo homes, and squirrels fill attics each fall
Seneca County.absent_or_rare: the white deer herd on the former Seneca Army Depot grounds is a managed attraction, not a nuisance service, and beavers and muskrats on the Montezuma edge are permit-gated

Steuben County.region: the south-central Southern Tier along Pennsylvania
Steuben County.nearest_metro: Elmira (about 35 miles east) and Rochester (about 75 miles north)
Steuben County.habitat_type: glass and manufacturing towns, vineyard hills, and farm valleys
Steuben County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold older Corning and Hornell blocks, groundhogs burrow the farm valleys, and raccoons and bats settle Bath and Keuka Lake homes and cottages
Steuben County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, and bobcats work the southern hills but are permit-gated; timber rattlesnakes occur in isolated Southern Tier pockets — safety and identification only

Suffolk County.region: the eastern two-thirds of Long Island
Suffolk County.nearest_metro: the New York City metro's eastern reach (about 60-100 miles to Manhattan)
Suffolk County.habitat_type: twin-fork vacation country, dense western suburbs, and protected pine barrens
Suffolk County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels dominate the western suburbs of Huntington, Babylon, and Islip, Norway rats hold the older downtowns and ferry and fishing ports, groundhogs burrow the farm and estate edges out east, and bats settle Southampton and East End summer homes
Suffolk County.absent_or_rare: Canada geese crowd the bayside parks and golf courses but need federal authorization for control, so goose work is deterrence only; DEC's Suffolk tree-clearing guidance for listed bats is a tree-work rule, not a building-exclusion rule

Sullivan County.region: the southern Catskills and Delaware River
Sullivan County.nearest_metro: the New York City metro's weekend reach (about 90 miles)
Sullivan County.habitat_type: resort and bungalow-colony country, camps, and small towns
Sullivan County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats settle bungalow colonies and seasonal homes around Monticello, Liberty, and Fallsburg that sit empty for months, and skunks den under camp porches each spring
Sullivan County.absent_or_rare: black bears are a Catskill fixture around trash and bird feeders and beavers work the Bashakill wetlands, but both are permit-gated DEC species

Tioga County.region: the Pennsylvania line of the eastern Southern Tier
Tioga County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm and garden edges from Owego to Candor, and raccoons and bats settle the river-village homes along the Susquehanna
Tioga County.absent_or_rare: black bears and beavers move through the southern hills and creek bottoms but need special DEC permits

Tompkins County.region: the southern end of Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes
Tompkins County.nearest_metro: Ithaca is itself the regional center; Syracuse is about 55 miles north
Tompkins County.habitat_type: a college city in a gorge-cut landscape with farm towns around
Tompkins County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold Ithaca's older downtown and student-rental blocks, raccoons and squirrels run the Cayuga Heights and Lansing canopy, groundhogs burrow the farm towns of Dryden and Groton, and bats return to big older homes each summer
Tompkins County.absent_or_rare: the eastern massasauga's only New York populations live in boggy wetlands in central New York west of the county — it is state-Endangered and federally Threatened, and any snake question here is identification and safety only; beavers on the inlet marshes are permit-gated

Ulster County.region: the west bank of the Hudson between the Catskills and the Highlands
Ulster County.nearest_metro: the New York City metro's weekend reach; Albany is about 55 miles north
Ulster County.habitat_type: a river city, college and farm towns, and mountain second-home country
Ulster County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold Kingston's older Rondout and uptown blocks, raccoons and squirrels settle second homes around Woodstock and Saugerties, groundhogs work the Wallkill valley farms, and bats colonize older New Paltz homes each summer
Ulster County.absent_or_rare: copperheads are documented in the county's rocky terrain (a DEC officer removed one in New Paltz) and timber rattlesnakes occur at the Catskill and Shawangunk edges — both are identification and safety matters only; Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in Ulster County, so bat colonies are identified before exclusion

Warren County.region: the southeastern Adirondacks and Lake George
Warren County.habitat_type: a small city, a resort lake, and mountain camp country
Warren County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats settle Lake George and Queensbury seasonal homes and Glens Falls older housing, often discovered only at spring opening
Warren County.absent_or_rare: black bears, beavers, fishers, and moose work the Adirondack interior but are DEC-managed; Indiana bat hibernacula are documented in Warren County, so bat work starts with identification

Washington County.region: the upper Hudson and Champlain valleys on the Vermont line
Washington County.nearest_metro: Albany (about 55 miles south) and Glens Falls (about 10 miles west)
Washington County.habitat_type: slate and dairy-farm valleys and canal towns
Washington County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the dairy-farm edges from Cambridge to Granville, and raccoons and bats settle Hudson Falls and Fort Edward homes
Washington County.absent_or_rare: beavers and black bears work the Batten Kill and eastern hills but need special DEC permits

Wayne County.region: the Lake Ontario shore between Rochester and Syracuse
Wayne County.habitat_type: canal towns and flat fruit and muck-farm country
Wayne County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the muck-farm and orchard edges, raccoons and bats settle Newark, Lyons, and Palmyra homes, and skunks den under farm porches
Wayne County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the canal and marsh bottoms but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Westchester County.region: directly north of New York City, between the Hudson River and Long Island Sound
Westchester County.nearest_metro: New York City (about 25 miles south of White Plains)
Westchester County.habitat_type: dense southern suburbs rising to wooded northern estate towns
Westchester County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold the older downtowns of Yonkers, Mount Vernon, and New Rochelle, raccoons and squirrels are relentless in the canopy suburbs from Scarsdale to Rye, and groundhogs, skunks, and bats are steady in the wooded northern towns around Pound Ridge and Croton
Westchester County.absent_or_rare: black bears wander the northern watershed woods and beavers work the Croton system, but both are DEC matters needing special permits; coyotes are present county-wide and are not a rabies-vector species in New York and not a removal booking

Wyoming County.region: the Genesee River headwaters between Buffalo and Rochester
natural_features: Genesee River gorge at Letchworth State Park
Wyoming County.habitat_type: dairy-farm valleys and the Letchworth gorge country
Wyoming County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs are a constant on the dairy farms around Warsaw, Perry, and Arcade, and raccoons and bats settle the village homes and farmhouses
Wyoming County.absent_or_rare: beavers, black bears, and fishers work the gorge and hill country but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

Yates County.region: the heart of the Finger Lakes on Keuka and Seneca lakes
Yates County.nearest_metro: Rochester (about 55 miles northwest) and Ithaca (about 40 miles southeast)
Yates County.habitat_type: vineyard and Mennonite farm country between two lakes
Yates County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the vineyard and farm edges, raccoons and bats settle Penn Yan homes and Keuka Lake cottages, and skunks work under farm porches
Yates County.absent_or_rare: beavers and muskrats press the lake outlets and marsh edges but are permit-gated and referred to DEC

St. Lawrence County.region: the St. Lawrence River valley and northwestern Adirondacks, the state's largest county by area
St. Lawrence County.nearest_metro: Watertown (about 70 miles southwest) and Plattsburgh (about 90 miles east)
St. Lawrence County.habitat_type: river ports, college towns, and vast farm and forest interior
St. Lawrence County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the dairy-farm landscape, raccoons and bats settle Ogdensburg, Massena, Potsdam, and Canton homes and northern camps, and squirrels fill attics each fall
St. Lawrence County.absent_or_rare: moose, black bears, beavers, fishers, and bobcats are established across the county's woods but are all DEC-managed, permit-gated species
